articles.title: Everybody’s macrodosing on microdramas
articles.summary: Following the news that Margot Robbie’s turn on Neighbours is fated to be clipped into a microdrama, Ima Caldwell explains the ins and outs of the rapidly growing medium of social media soap operas, werewolves and all. 10 chaotic questions with Michael Theo: ‘I want to be on Dancing with the Stars!
body: Leading questions: ‘My sister-in-law is nearly 40 but cannot handle losing at board games. What can I do?’

Ima Caldwell: Television distilled, for your dopamine-fiending pleasure! A microdrama is usually an episodic series filmed (or reframed) in portrait orientation, for phone screens. Each instalment clocks in at around 60-90 seconds and they’re aired to social media and on specialised microdrama streaming apps. They’re generally packed with enough plot twists to make daytime television look like slow cinema. One producer described them as “soap operas on cocaine”. Maybe the sort of thing you’d end up watching drunk at 2am.

Alyx: I downloaded ReelShort the other day and was kind of shocked at the content. Forced marriage mafia plotlines; Secretly Pregnant by the Homeless Billionaire. It basically looked like the greatest hits (and misses) of Kindle Unlimited’s alpha male romance charts. Is the Neighbours microdrama going to be that hectic?

articles.title: I hibernate in a couch lasagna beneath this microwaveable heated blanket
articles.summary: Like Linus with his blankie, Bearaby’s Lounger is my constant companion when the weather gets brisk. My wife swears by weighted blankets to sleep – and now I understand why. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I n the early months of the pandemic, I enjoyed a brief flirtation with a 15lb weighted blanket from Amazon, but eventually abandoned it because it was impossible to launder and also sort of ugly. A few years later, I tried a different option – the sleep brand Bearaby’s flagship weighted blanket, an almost-but-not-quite-right solution that worked but eventually became cumbersome. In a frenzied afternoon spent deep cleaning, I set that one aside and eventually heaved it into the back of my sister’s Jeep for her.

Even though those two blankets didn’t stick, I still wanted something similar – just not ugly, large or hard to handle. Though I run hot and my apartment is often a furnace in the winter, my ideal leisure situation is enjoying the crisp air blowing in through a cracked window from the cozy and warm nest I’ve made on my sofa. Bearaby came to my rescue once more with the Lounger, a combination heated and weighted blanket that has been in my life for three years and is now my favorite thing in my apartment once winter sets in.
points: Like Linus with his blankie, Bearaby’s Lounger is my constant companion when the weather gets brisk.

articles.title: A-listers and AI stylists: how high-street brands are staging a fashion comeback
articles.summary: Gap, M&S, Topshop and more are taking a leaf from luxury label playbooks to satisfy savvier generation of shoppers. High street brands that boomed in the noughties before the squeeze of both sustainably minded consumers and the rise of ultra-cheap online labels are staging a comeback.
body: This time, rather than focusing solely on trend-led affordable designs, the names familiar to any shopper are courting luxury fashion, A-list collaborations and enhanced services in an attempt to engage consumers.

Think Gap’s new collection with Victoria Beckham. Or Marks & Spencer showcasing a covetable catwalk collection at London fashion week with celebrities including Joan Collins and assorted gen Z Gallaghers in attendance, then making it available to buy immediately, with half of the pieces under £50. Topshop relaunched last year and now has concessions in 30 John Lewis stores, as well as the luxury retailer Liberty.

Lisa Illis, the head of design at M&S, describes their recent catwalk show as “making the buzz of London fashion week accessible to everyone”. She says “more fashion-informed seasonal collections” have seen the number of under-35s shopping at the retailer increase 16% year on year.

The Hollywood stylist Law Roach, whose clients include Zendaya, has been appointed stylist-in-residence at Asos, where his influence will be felt not just in advertising campaigns, but also through his suggestions on different items from across the site to wear together.
points: Gap, M&S, Topshop and more are taking a leaf from luxury label playbooks to satisfy savvier generation of shoppers.

articles.title: Let’s Give a Big Hand for Heidi Klum’s 2026 Halloween Costume
articles.summary: This year, the queen of Halloween transformed herself into a giant replica of her own hand. “I thought it would be funny and bizarre to take something so familiar and twist it.”
body: The star began ideating on the concept about a year ago—even before her 2025 Halloween bash, when she dressed up as Medusa. “Sometimes an idea comes to me very early, and other times I'm still figuring things out closer to Halloween,” says Klum. “I remember trying to explain it to my costume designer, Mike Marino, and he basically told me that he needed to focus on Medusa first! But it stayed in the back of my mind, and I knew I wanted to bring it to life this year.”

As usual, Klum worked her go-to team of special effects artists to bring her delightfully-kooky vision to life. Mike Marino, her right-hand man, led the work with his ProRenFX team. They began by taking a look at Klum’s very own hand for design inspiration. “[Mike] has all of these scans of my body, so he was able to use those to create an exact replica of my hand,” says Klum. “We wanted everything to be as realistic as possible—the anatomy, the veins, the muscles, all the little details that make a hand look like a real hand.”

articles.title: 21 Easy Weeknight Dinners for November
articles.summary: Like creamy fondue beans, stuffing-crusted fish, and more cozy meals for chilly nights.
body: As daylight dwindles and the November chill settles in, dinner calls for something cozy. Think chicken thighs nestled into caramelized onions, pasta slicked with brown butter, and hearty soups that practically demand a hunk of crusty bread. It’s time to lean into comfort food.

The good news? You don’t need to spend your whole Sunday cooking to make dinner feel special, so you’ll have plenty of time for that When Harry Met Sally rewatch. These 21 easy weeknight dinners deliver all the comfort without the commitment. There’s a three-ingredient pumpkin soup, gochujang chicken that gets a quick blast under the broiler, and a smoky one-pan pasta made with pantry staples. Plus a few Thanksgiving -adjacent flavors—sage, stuffing, squash—because the holiday is right around the corner.
points: Like creamy fondue beans, stuffing-crusted fish, and more cozy meals for chilly nights.

articles.title: 13 Books That Changed Comedian, Author, and Drag King Murray Hill’s Life
articles.summary: Hill’s new memoir, “Showbiz!: My Life as a Middle-Aged Man,” is out now from Gallery Books.
body: Hollywood is a strange and mysterious place, even for those who have operated within its orbit for decades. But author, comedian, and drag king Murray Hill’s new memoir, Showbiz!: My Life as a Middle-Aged Man (Gallery Books), sheds an alternately moving and hilarious light on “the industry,” charting Hill’s rise from a fraught New England childhood to a career starring in New York and Boston cabaret shows and appearing on television series including Somebody, Somewhere, Life & Beth, and Elsbeth.
In the latest edition of Vogue ’s Required Reading series, Hill shares a selection of books that have inspired his own memoir and seen him through the ups and downs of Hollywood life.

Kathleen Hanna is a punk-rock icon, feminist trailblazer, and one of my dearest friends. She’s spent her life making noise, breaking rules, and telling the establishment to beat it. What I love about this book is how she writes about the messy, painful, and hilarious realities behind being a revolutionary. She built her own stage, grabbed the microphone, and started a movement. She is my forever inspiration.

articles.title: Gigi Hadid Cut the Ribbon on Her Fourth Guest in Residence Store with Cashmere, Caviar, and Caricatures
articles.summary: Model and founder Gigi Hadid, clad in a shrunken top and tartan skirt, celebrated the debut of her label’s fourth U.S. store—and its very first uptown address.
body: The first surprise was a trio of pretzels twisted into the letters G, I, and R at the entrance. Inside, florists busied themselves preparing custom arrangements, a three-piece band played beneath a sloped skylight, and a caricature artist stationed near the bar had guests voguing for their portraits and later comparing their likenesses.

Martini glasses were filled with one of two things: martinis, of course, but also cigarettes. Meanwhile, caviar in every conceivable configuration made the rounds: atop passed blinis, with potato chips and crème fraîche at a help-yourself station, and even crowning freshly baked potatoes.
